text:
ina: Spike idea: support manifestless progressive hydration driven by a lightweight shard-registry service. goal: avoid embedding complex phase arrays in every bundle and let the runtime subscribe to hints.

rahul: interesting. how does registry differ from existing manifest phases? is it just moving config to a service? :thinking_face:

ina: yes but with a twist — registry exposes time-windowed warmup hints computed from live traffic (hot shards, prefix affinity) and a stable shard-uuid map. bundles still declare shard uuids, but no phase array. loader calls registry.subscribe(bundle_id) and gets prioritized shards + TTL.

cesar: i like runtime-driven hints. benefits: we can evolve warmup heuristics without changing bundle files. downsides: network dependency during start. what if registry is down?

jo: fallback: bundle includes a tiny defaults file (hot-shards: top-5 by heuristic) if registry unreachable. loader should fall back to index-first warmup in that case. also: registry responses must be signed to prevent tampering.

rahul: security note: sign with the same KMS we use for manifests. registry should publish a signature and a versioned watermark. loader verifies and rejects stale hints.

ina: perf model: optimistic background hydrate for low-priority shards, synchronous hydrate for shards that registry marks "immediate". if a request references a cold shard, behavior options: block-with-timeout, serve-via-compat-model, or abort+retry. we should pick 2 via config.

cesar: metric proposals: registry_hints_applied_rate, cold_shard_block_rate, compat_fallback_rate, and percent_of_requests_with_partial_response. add tracing: span name "shard:hydrate:<uuid>".

jo: operationally we need canary semantics: registry can roll hot-list changes gradually across availability zones. loader must accept a target_priority and a max-delta-per-minute so we don't thrash IO.

ina: implementation sketch: 1) shard-registry service (read-only for runtime) 2) loader subscribe API: subscribe(bundle_id)->[ {shard_uuid,priority,reason,expires_at,sig} ] 3) ensure_shard(shard_uuid, opts) primitive in loader 4) signed hints + manifest_version compatibility check.

rahul: a few questions: how do we map shards -> logical layer boundaries for kvcache lookups? registry should include optional "layer_hint" string so loaders can co-locate IO when beneficial.

cesar: agree. also we should add a tiny audit log in registry for changes so perf-sim can replay warmup decisions.

warmup-bot: registry-spike perf-sim complete (bundle=large-gptx, strategy=registry-driven): median cold-hit latency +18ms, 95p +210ms, mem-peak -9%. report: https://ci.example/reports/3743210000

ina: nice numbers. next: I'll sketch a minimal registry proto and a PoC loader adapter. jo can you draft the security signing flow? rahul can you own perf sims?

jo: on it. will sketch SIG format and KMS policy.

rahul: will run sims against staging with two fallback modes: compat-model and block-with-retry.

cesar: i'll prepare dashboards for proposed metrics and add alerts for compat_fallback_rate >0.3% sustained.

ina: thanks all. we'll aim to land registry PoC behind a feature flag. :rocket:
